Posted March 4, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

What impact do cannabis friendly policies have on the quality of life in the world's major cities? The international personnel firm, Mercer Human Resource Consulting, has issued its 2002 report comparing the quality of life and personal safety in the world's major cities, and the results confound the prohibitionists.

Although there is no mention of cannabis, it happens that cannabis friendly cities crowd the top ten. Zurich, in cannabis friendly Switzerland, was first and Vancouver was second.
See
Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.

Vienna, where the police stopped arresting for cannabis possession in 1998, tied Vancouver for second, as did Geneva.
See
Half A Million Viennese Have Tried Cannabis; Police Have Stopped Arresting Users

Amsterdam ranked tenth in the world for overall quality of life, beating drug free Stockholm.
See
Analysis By Dutch Center Shows
" Claims Regarding Effectiveness Of The Swedish Drug Policy Cannot Be Proven. "
and
Why The Drug Czar Went To Sweden First; This Is The Prohibitionist Ideal.

In DEAland, very cannabis friendly San Francisco was the highest ranked city at number 20. It is also important to note that Giuliani's police state, which is being sold around the world as a triumph of get tough law and order policies ranks lower (64th) than liberal San Francisco (40th) for personal safety.
See
Giuliani's Police State Like the Marijuana Prohibition That He Loves Is A Counterproductive Fraud. 3 Articles.

The lowest scoring city in North America is Washington D.C, ranked 107 (score 85).

The capital city of the global drug war is the capital of violence.

Mercer says, Canadian cities are the safest in North America, due to strict law enforcement and low crime rates. Calgary, Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver share joint 25th position with a score of 113.5.

John Walters should remember that fact or be reminded of it the next time he lectures Canada on its cannabis policies.

The point here is simply that liberal cannabis policies do not detract from the quality of life or personal safety. On the contrary, it would appear that social tolerance and the intelligent use of police resources improves both.

This survey offers very important lessons for civic leaders and politicians who have been lied to for years about the impact that the legalization of cannabis would have on their cities.
